newsitem.title: UK: Euro veg oils quietly mixed ahead of USDA report.
newsitem.headline: Euro veg oils quietly mixed ahead of USDA report.

text.p: Midday European vegetable oil prices were mixed on a thin market at midday on Friday ahead of the USDA crop report due around 1230 GMT.
"Both sides of the market are very thin, with most people hoping the USDA report will give the market some direction," said one trader.
News that the Philippines Central Bank would allow the peso to move in a wider range against the dollar was seen as having only limited impact on coconut oil prices in Europe.
"It will take a few days to sort out, but in the end I think the impact will be minimal," said one trader.
Palm oil was quiet and little changed with refiner buying and selling dominating the market.
"The same refiner has been in the market, selling nearby olein and buying forward, said one trader.
No activity was reported in soft oils ahead of the USDA report with buyers not very keen owing to the ideal growing conditions in the U.S.
At midday crude palm oil cif Europe was $2.50 up after Sep traded at $506 a tonne cif.

Among products RBD palm oil was unchanged to $2.50 down while olein was $5 up to unchanged after Aug traded at $525 and $527.50, Oct/Dec at $522.50 and Jan/Mar at $522.50 and $524 a tonne fob Malaysian ports.
Coconut oil was $7.50 up to $5 down while palmkernel oil was $5 higher with no business reported.
Dutch soy oil offers were 0.25 guilders down to unchanged while rape oil was unchanged to 1.25 guilders higher.
